speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) whether there are plans to enhance the information on LCD systems above MRT train doors by (i) displaying both the current stop and a route map for easier reference by commuters at all times and (ii) ensuring consistent information display across all trains and lines; and (b) if so, when are these enhancements expected to be implemented.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) since the implementation of the LCD display systems, how many feedback reports have all the train operators and LTA received regarding the clarity of information on the LCD display systems above train doors; and (b) which MRT line received the most of such feedback.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In addition to the LCD screens located above the doors, commuters are provided with travel information, such as the current and next station, through in-train announcements and ceiling level displays in the middle of train cabins.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: I ask these Parliamentary Questions as I frequently commute via the MRT.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: As a commuter, it is not always easy to identify where exactly I am on the MRT route, especially when the train is crowded and even more so for a wheelchair user, where the eye-level is a lot lower.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: So, the LCD display, as you pointed out, is not consistent across the train lines.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: In my opinion, ensuring better user interface should be a priority and is potentially not too complex an issue to solve.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: So, I would just like to ask the Senior Parliamentary Secretary if there are any challenges to make this information more consistently clear across the train lines and whether or not we can share a more concrete timeline of when to expect them.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han
text: I just want to say that as a commuter and a wheelchair user, it is not sufficient because it is quite important to be able to know exactly where you are at all times.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han
text: And then, the East-West Line tends to show the station name quite clearly, I think in the rotating information, but not in the context of where you are on the route map.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han
text: So, let us say if you were dozing off on the train and you look up, it is not immediately clear and you may miss a stop.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han
text: And it is even more so if you have mobility challenges and I just wanted to raise that.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han
text: I would be happy to take this also offline to discuss how we can enhance this.
